div.head: Bank Quay Recs. v. Emmanuel.
div.p: Bank Quay Recs. v. Emmanuel.

This match was played at Lovely-lane, and after sthe' recent heavy rains the ground was in a very bad condition. The following players lined out, under Referee T. Pittam :—Bank Quay Roes.: W. Bushell; C. Berry and W. Tay- lor; T. Worrall, W. Lagar and A. Booth; H. !Eccleston, D. Deakin, D. Bradshaw, J."'Davies and E. Green. Emmanuel T. Knight; T. Pot- ter and J. Irdana; Wainwright, J. Hatton and J. O'Brien; J. Singleton, A. Carter, J. Isher- wood, G. Caldwell and J. W. All& The Recs. won the toss, and Isherwood kicked off. The home team, getting possession, began to press very strongly, but met with a fine defence by Knight and Hatton, who kept them at bay. Not to be denied, the Recs. came down on the visitors' citadel again, and Deakin scored' with a shot that gave Knight no chance to save. From the centre kia,k the Emmanuel boys carried the game into the home half, but poor combination by their forwards allowed several good chances to go by, but they still continued to keep the home. defence busy. Caldwell netted the ball ! from a grand centre by Allen. Even play fol- lowed up to the interval, which , arrived with the score one goal each. The -Bees. began to play a fine combination game, and severely tested 'Knight in the visit- ors' goal. He made ~several very smart clear- ,ances. The heavy ground began to tell on the visiting team, and they fell away in their dis- play, and Dyer increased the score from a scramble in goal. After this reverse the Recs. monopolised the• play, but they were lacking in the finish towards goal, but eventually Eccles- ton, by a good individual effort, scored the third goal for the Recs. The ground now began to have the appearance 'of a quagmire rather than a football pitch, and combination was at a dis- count. Long kicking was indulged in by both teams, and at the final whistle the game stood: Bank Quay Recs., three goals; Emmanuel, one goal.

div.head: Fairfield United v. Excelsior.
div.p: Fairfield United v. Excelsior.

This match was played at Odor\ d-lane, when a good number of each club's supporters was present, and the players lined out as follows : Fairfield United: Bibby; Rowlands and Wood- house; Rigby, Gregory and Shelmerdine; Col- lins, Gleave, Hodge, Bebbington and Oxley. Ex- celsior: Rigby; Morris and Holmes; Hunt, Spencer and O'Neil; Cox, Welsby, Pritchard, Leah and Walker. Referee, G. Bamber. The visitors won the toss, kicked towards the rail- way end, and at once set an attack on the home goal. Cox was successful in beating Rigby with ,a grand shot. Encouraged by this success, the visitors stormed the home goal, and Walker, doing the needful, added a second goal. Nettled by these reverses, the home team played more briskly, and made an advance on the visitors' goal, but Morris and Holmes were not to be de- feated. and the ball was transferred to the home goal, when Leah scored a third point. The home forwards now began to assert themselves, and it was only by good defensive play by Morris that they were kept from scoring. The Excelsiors, not to be outdone, made another raid and Pritchard scored' a fourth goal, which was the outcome of a good piece of combination by the whole of the Excelsior forwards. The play now settled down in midfield, and at half-time the visitors were leading by four ,goals to nil. The game restarted in spirited fashion. The home forwards made desperate attempts to re- duce the arrears, and gave the visitors' defence an anxious time, but they did not waver in their play and Morris cleared with a fine kick. Play was transferred to the opposite end. Morris handled in the dreaded area, and from the en- suing penalty, Efodger scored for the home team. Even play followed, and the ball travelled quickly from end to end, until Walker hit the 1 crossbar with a grand shot. From the rebound 1 O'Neil added a fifth goal. This reverse seemed 1 to have an effect on the home team, and their I play suffered, and it was only by good defensive play by Woodhouse and Rowlands that no fur- ther score took place, a very keen game ending in favour of the Excelsiors by five goals to Fair- field United, one goal.
FRIENDLY MATCH. Great Sankey v. Widnes County Reserve.

Notwithstanding the fact that Widnes County sent their reserve team to Penketh on Satur- day, they had a powerful side out, and the meet- ing brought together some 300 enthusiasts. The teams lined out as follows :—Great Sankey: J. Davenport; E. Glover and R. Stephens; H. Ditchfield, J. Ditchfield and 11. Payne; E. Dar- lington, E. Ditchfield, T. Illidge, S. Poulter and A. Houghton. Widnes County Reserve: A. Forshaw ; W. Hesketh and F. Hesketh ; J. Mor- ris, A. Brown and J. Hughes; J. Foster, J. Dale, H. Freeman, T. Leadbetter and J. McAllister. Referee, Mr. R. Rule, Warrington. The visitors opened the game very briskly, and were soon in the home goalmouth, and J. Davenport was luck.,v in clearing the danger. At the other end A. Houghton centred, but T. Illidge failed at the critical moment. The County right wing broke away, but H. Payne checked, and put his forwards in possession. They could not, however, get through, and the Ball was transferred to the home half, where R. Stephens cleared with a huge punt. This enabled the Sankey left to work a good position and S. Poulter scored with a fine drive, after six minutes' play. This defeat roused the County, and they took the Sankey defence by surprise. T. Leadbetter equalised some few minutes afterwards. Both teams were playing good football, each defence being tested in turn. J. Ditchfield worked a good position and gave to E. Darlington, who shot weakly. The County pressed very strongly, and E. Glover made a grand clearance-from J. Foster, and 11. Payne forced a corner, which came to nothing. When the interval arrived the score stood at one goal each.

On the resumption A. Forshaw was called upon to save froth S. Poulter, and then E. Dar- lington scored a second goal, which went in off W. Hesketh. From a free kick R. Stephens put the ball over the bar. The more the visitors pressed the more they found the home defence sound. E. Darlington was playing much better than in the first half, and one of his centres was just missed by S. Poulter. The visitors' left wine raced away, but R. Stephens proved a stumbling block and relieved the situation. From a throw-in E. Darlington got possession, but F. Hesketh robbed him just in time. To- wards the close play became very exciting, and H. Ditchfield just shaved the post, after A. Forshaw had punched clear. H. Freeman made play on the left, but E. Glover went to the rescue and cleared. A free kick. taken by H. Ditchfield, was nicely placed, and A. Houghton nut in a fine shot, which A. Forshaw saved. Final: Great Sankey, two goals; Widnes County. Reserve, one goal.

div.head: St. Mary's v. St. George's.
div.p: St. Mary's v. St. George's.

- - . The abilVe was played at Arpley. St. Mary's won the toss and decided to kick with the wind at their backs. Play opened very evenly; both ends being visited without effect. The home team were now having the best-of the game, and lost many chances through excitement. St. George's began to play an improved,game, and transferred the leather into the home quar- ters, and Hands scored from a centre by Roberts. At half-time the score was: St. George's, one goal; St. Mary's, nil. The home centre kicked off in the second por-

tion, and the ball ,was at once carried into the opponents'. area, but was .driven hall by Phillips. St. George's now began to have the upper hand, and made a rush on the. home goal and one df the defending backs kicked through his own goal. St. Mary's could notonake headway against against the George's defence. Hands scored again from a centre by Roberta. The visitors continued to have the best of, the game; but no further scoring took place. Result: St. George's, three goals; St. Mary's, none.,

Emmanuel v. Paddington. • On the Albion ground. Paddington won the toss and played with the wind. The visitors broke away in style and W. Knight put in a fine centre, which came to nothing. Following- this, the visitors were doing all the attacking. The Paddington forwards came in dashing stylo, but could not •break down the sound defence of Newton and Hughes. The visitors forced their way to the home goal-mouth, and from a centre by W. Knight, S. Roberts did the needful. Half- time: Emmanuel, one goal; Paddington, nil. Resuming, Emmanuel were the first away, and a well-judged kick by Ayres ended in F. Hughes scoring. After this Paddington fell away, and

a nice piece of combination between Banner, P. Hughes and Knight ended in the latter putting in a lovely centre, for Berry, to score a third. The visitors again attacked 'and S. Roberts scored. Shortly afterwards Robert's added hit% third goal. The game ended in a capital win for .Emmanuel by five goals to nil. • For the winners, T. Hughes, Ayres and Banner' were the pick, and for the losers E. Vickers and J. Hepherd played .•well. • •
F'adgate United V. Stockton Heath.

This friendly fixture was played at Padgate. The visitors had the best of the game during the, first fifteen .minutes, but could not pierce the home- defence, the best effort being' a- shot by Jones, which hit the cross-bar. The home team next made an attack, and in attempting to save a shot from the home right wing. Sim- cock mulled the ball and allowed it to roll over the line. From the centre kick the visitors went away and Smith equalised from a neat pass by Jones. The tome team made another raid on the visitors' goal, and gained the' lead, and Padgate was leading at half-time by two goals against one. On resuming, the visitors were soon in the home quarters. Taylor received' from Smith and equalised. Shortly after the home team was ahead again through a mistake by the goalkeeper. The visitors now put more energy into their game. WoodwaTd scored from a throw-in, Magill got another from a well-placed corner, and Smith scored his third goal of the match just before the finish: Result: Stockton Heath, six goals; Padgate United, three goals.

Grappenhall St. Wilfrid's v: Old Botelerians. At Grappenhall. The home team soon •forced ' matters, and from a corner Ford headed over the bar. Hampson and 'Richards were just too wide with good shots. The visitors, however, soon got going, only to be pulled up by Evans and Booth. The home team, not to be denied, pressed, and from a good centre by H. Parr, Thomas gave the visitors' custodian no chance. Grappenhall, stimulated by this success, again took the ball to the visitors' end, but, owing to fine defensive play on the part of Hankey and Venn, in goal, were unable to ,score. A 'well- placed corner by .the Botelerians was put through the home goal by a Grappenhall player, half-time arriving with the score one all. - On resumption, the home team pressed hard, only to be repulsed ..by Hankey. A penalty to Grappenhall failed to bring them any success. Duckworth got away with the ball, centring very well, and Maclntyre made no mistake, beating the home goalie with a fine shot. Play 'here became of a give-and-take nature, and the home team soon equalised through the medium of F. Parr, and with 15 minutes to go, Ford scored for Grappenhall, filom a nicely-placed corner by Hampson, the "Saints" thus win-, 'ling by 3-2. For the Botelerians, Venn, in goal; Hankey, right back; and Maclntyre played well, whilst Ford, Hampson, Booth and Evans were, the pick of the home team.

div.head: TEAMS AND MATCHES FOR TO-DAY.
div.p: TEAMS AND MATCHES FOR TO-DAY.

Latchford to-day have to make the journey to Heatley to meet Oughtrington United in the first round of the North Cheshire Senior Cup Competition. It is expected there will be a keen fight for victory. Interest is added‘by the fact that Onghtrington United beat Lostock Gralam on Saturday in the League Competi- tion, and this alone should give the home team more confidence-when they take the field against their old rivals. The following players will represent Latchford: P. A. Kite; J. C. Bardsley and W. G. Robinson; P. Downs, E. Webb and J. Carter; S. Smith, W. Ir.. Challinor, J. Lees, S. Siddall and W. Taylor. Reserve, H. Stubbs. The players are travelling by the 1.18 train from Latchford; kick off 2.4.5. The Stockton Heath Club will revive an °old- time rivalry when they meet their neighbours from Daresbury on the West-avenue ground. The following will represent the home club: Simeoek; Gosling and Woodward; Magill, Denny and Gifford; Gerrard, Lockhart, .Jones, Smith and Taylor. The Adult School and Orford St. John's, both members of - the Warrington and District League, First and Second Divisions respectively, having no League engagement, have arranged a friendly fixture, to be played in Victoria Park on Saturday. LATCHFORD SENIORS WELL BEATEN. Latchford First visited Bowdon on Saturday, and were well beaten by'five goals to two. The visitors Could hardly expect to run the home team -very. close, and on the whole made a very creditable show, as they' are the only team to score .twice against Bowdon this season. Latchford were the first to score, which they did soon after the commencement, a beautifully combined movement ending in Travis scoring with a good shot. After this the Bowdon for- wards played up well, scoring three times before the interval. In the second • half Bowdon scored twice to Latchford's one goal, shot by Colton. _ _ _ _ - .
Throughout the game the Latchford halires were subdued by the Bowdon forwards, Who played well to a man, while the forwards had the worst Of the argument with the Bowdon defence.
Fletcher played well for Latchford, and was the only outstanding defender.
LATCHFORD RESERVES DRAW.

Latchford Second were at home to Bowdon "A," and a very enjoyable game 'ended in a goalless draw. From the bully-off Bowdon took up the aggressive, and for the first quarter of an hour they gave the Latchford defence a warm time, having several shots at goal, none of which, however, were successful. Then play was transferred for a time to the visitors' goal, and Latchford pressed so much that Bowdon had to concede three or four corners, before get- ting the ball out, of the danger zone. About this time Bowdon's outside right was much in the picture, he putting in some fine first time centres, one of which the Bowdon centre, picking up, crashed the ball against the

For Latchford, Banks was the "outstanding man, his stick work being a treat to watch, while Starkey, on the right wing, did several good runs, and had hard lines on at least two occasions in not going through and scoring on his own. The full-backs also gave a much-im- proved display. In fairness to Bowdon, it should be stated that they played a man short throughout the game, but when it is remembered that they have only lost twice out of the last 60 games played, one cannot help but think that Latch- ford put up a very good performance.

div.head: Crosfield's Recreation Meet with Igefeaty Latchford Secure a 5-0 Win With a Weak Team,
div.p: Crosfield's Recreation Meet with Igefeaty Latchford Secure a 5-0 Win With a Weak Team,
INCIDENTS IN WARRINGTON LEAGUE GAMES.

Mobberley Amateurs paid .a visit to the Thel- wall enclosure and had to return defeated by five goals.to none,-,although the Latchford•team, Was below usual strength, Bardsley being unable to turn out owing to business engagements, and Green, another amateur of repute; was expected to turn out for the home club, but wired off at the last moment. The services of their useful reserves had to be requisitioned, and it speaks well for their play that the club were able to gain such a fine victory. The visitors were not the Mobberley of old. Crosfield's Recreation made the journey to the. Bowdon Vale Club, and had to return de- feated. The result did not surprise their sup- porters, as it i& well known that the Bowdon Club allow very few points" to be taken froni: them at their own ground. WARRINGTON LEAGUE NOTES.

In the Warrington and District League, the juniors of Crosfield's Rec. were successful in de- feating the team from Daresbury, but there was a great deal of luck about the. result, as the winning goal had scarcely sufficient speed be- hind it to travel between the posts. Three of the visitors allowed the ball to pass them, ex- pecting the other to take it, and thus it made the -difference of a point to their- record-in the League chart. The ground at Folly-lane was in a terrible condition, and unless there are some efforts made to improve the playing pitch the pros- peas are that the club will not be able to play their cup .tie,on it when Ogden's have to appear in the Liverpool Cup ties on the 22nd of this month.

The Adult School team met the Divex in Vic- toria Park in the League tournament, and the game ended in a complete rout of the visitors, their play being of a ragged description, and not of the style that adds to the score sheet of a club.. The scores ihat are . being piled up against them so far proves that they are weak both in defence as well as in attack. „Orford Barracks played their return fixture with Weston at Orford, when their won by three goals to none. In the first encounter the game was drawn, and thus 'Orford Barracks are very well satisfied with the result, having obtained 'three out of the four points. The game was full of exciting incidents, Hanley being in great form at .centre-half, Trafford and Procter doing well among the forwards. Nancollis,. the visitors' cUstodian, was a host in himself, being ably assisted by his backs. Fairfield United and the -Excelsiors met at Orford-road, and a good match was witnessed, and resulted in the defeat of the home team. Woodhouse Was the best man on the home side, and was nicely supported by Gregory and Row- lands, Whilst the visitors played well all round.

The Stockton Heath and Ya-i-r#e)4l match was well contested during the first -portion, when the visitors were only one goal- down, but the home team overplayed them during the gi3cond half, adding three more goals. . St. Barnabas' and Emmanuel met at Lovely- lane, and what would otherwise have been a good game was spoilt by the wretched condition of the ground. The home team were more accustomed to the heavy conditions under which they played, and won the match by three goals to one. Knight did some good work in the visit- ors' goal. Hatton -also played 'well at centre- half. The home team were best represented by Bradshaw, Dyer and Deakin. The Great Sankey' team, havingipo League en- gagement on, played a friendly With Widnes County reserves at Penketh. The game .was keenly contested all through, and the earnest- ness which both teams showed was greatly ap- preciated by the spectators. There was not a slack moment during the whole game. Padgate- United. entertained Stockton Heath, in a friendly at Padgate, where a pleasant game was witnessed. The visitors were inclined to treat their opponents rather lightly during the earlier stages, and later on had to show their abilities to enable them to win.
By "Linesman"

Forster, F. Forster, 11. De Prez, Adams and Cartwright. The visitors won the toss and de- fended the railway. godl. Beddall kicked off. The home forwarAs"went to the visitors' goal,. and Pagett scored in the first minute for the home team. The visitors retaliated and Made an attack on the home 6411 and forced a corner off Tindall. The ball was nicely, placed, and Wells cleared, the danger. Pagett shot just wide of the post for the home team, and at the other end Y. Forster shot over the bar, when in a good position for scoring. The home team were hav- ing the best of the exchanges, when Cash ap- peared and completed , the -visitors' team. A fine shot from Kimberley, the home centre-half, skimmed the bar from long range. The visitors now improved and had. more of the game, and; gained several-corners, but were not successful. ; The home.team made an attack on,the visitors'. citadel, where Ravenscroft made several- smart ' saves. Cash had to concede a corner to the homesters, which proved fruitless.. Half-time: Crosfield's, one goal; Daresbury, nil. On resuming, the home team invaded the visit- ors' half, but were driven back by the defenders, and the ball was taken into the home quarters, a long shot being sent in, H. De Prez caught the ball on the rebound, and made the scores equal. Play was not of a very exciting nature, the homesters having the best of the exchanges. Ravenscroft brought , off several . good saves, while the visitors paid an occasional visit into the home half. Ellison had to bestir himself to clear the ball, and shortly after had to repeat this feat, from which play was transferred to the visitors' goal: Rowlands sent in a slow shot and scored a very easy goal. Just before the finish Beddall was unfortunate in getting hurt in attempting to shoot, and had to be carried off, having strained the cartilage of his knee. No more scoring took place. Result: Crosfield's Reserves, two goals; Daresbury, one goal.

div.head: Adult School v. Divex.
div.p: Adult School v. Divex.

The above match -IN:as played in Victeria Park. The players turned out, under the Supervision of Referee Rushton, as follows :—Adult School: Welsby ; Garnett and Spilsbury ; Ridyard, Hunter and Spencer; Rhodes, Rowe, Leigh, Ban- ner and Craik. Divex r Hunt; Pento7d and Flute; Rennie, Ashworth, and Jackson; Leigh, Lightfoot, Deonfield, Savage and Roberts. The home team won the toss, Deonfield started' foc the visitors, and the opening exchanges were in midfield. Rhodes received the ball on the wing and passing to Rowe, the latter shot from twenty yards range and scored the first goal. Hunt niis- fielded the' ball and allowed it to roll over the line. Frem the centre kick the home forwards swarmed roUnd .the visitors' goal, and Leigh, sending in a slow shot, Hunt,, the visitors' goal- keeper, was at fault again. End-to-end play fol- lowed, and the visitors were now having more of the game; Penfold, doing some fine defensive play for the Divez,' had to concede a corner. From the flag kick Rennie- relieved with a big punt, and Hunter, by good play ;enabled Rhodes to score the third goal far the home team. No further score took place, up to half-time, when the Adult School were leading by ,three goals to nil. •

On resuming the visitors appeared to lose heart, and the game suffered, conseqUently the home team had the game all their own way, and Leigh scored the fourth goal. On several occa- sions off-side against the School lads spoilt good openings, and Rowe quickly added three more goals. -The visitors were .now .playing a hope-. less game and Craig scored No. 8, while Banner scored two further goals. The home team won -easily. Result: Adult School, ten goals; Divex, nil. For the Divex, Flute, Penfold and Roberts were the best, and Hunter was most prominent for the School, Ridyard running him close for honours.

div.p: Orfcrd Barracks v. Weston.

. . The return fixture between these clubs took place on the Soldiers' ground, when the follow- ing players turned out, under Referee Howell : Orford Barracks: Morrison; Stevens and Lon- nen ; Callow, Hanley and Pressland ; Campbell, Hicks, Forshaw, Procter and Trafford. Weston,. Nancollis; Oldfields and Burns; Hazlehurst, Aspey and Smith; Kirkham, Conway, Flanagan, Hulse and Molyneux. The Weston captain was successful in naming the coin; and the Soldiers kicked off with the sun in their face. Forshaw .at once worked his way towards the visitors' goal, when Burns relieved the danger, and Kirkham raced away on the right, and made a capital centre, which Flanagan failed to utilise. A fine bout of passing between Hanley, Procter and Trafford ended in the latter shooting past Nancollis after ten minutes' play. The visitors now took the leather into the home quarters, but could not break do the Soldiers' defence, Hanley being a thorn in the visitors' attack. Callow set Campbell going with a fine pass, and he ,centred from the touch-line. Forshaw being in an off-side position, the ball was transferred to the other end, only to be returned by the home backs, and Nancollis, in the visitors' goal, had his work cut out to stave off defeat. Un- fortunately, after fine defensive play, Hazle- hurst headed through his own goal, a.nd the Sol- diers were two up. The Soldiers continued to have the best-of the game, and were awarded a penalty for hands, but owing to an infringement the kick had to be taken a second time, and Nancollis saved the shot. half-time: Barracks, two goals; Weston, nil. On resuming, Forshaw, Hicks and Campbell made a fine run down the field, only to be driven back by Oldfield and Burns, who were kicking finely. Aspey, by good play, set Kirkham off, and he made ,a fine swinging pass oust to Maly- neux, who Nade an effort to score, but Morrison was safe in goal. The Visitors were awarded a penalty for foul play, but Morrison cleared, and Procter raced away and centring to Forshaw, he made a poor attempt:with his shot. The home half-backs were feeding their forwards very well, and the visitors' defence was plied with plenty of work, but Procter found the net, and the game ended: Orford Barracks, three goals; Weston, nil.

NORTH CHESHIRE LEAGUE. Latchford V. Mobberley Amateurs:

This match, in the 'North Cheshire League competition, was played at Thelwall-lane before a good crowd of spectators. - The visitors were well represented, but the home team had to play thEee of their reserves. The Latchford players were: Kite; Robinson and Stubbs; Downs, Webb and Siddall; Smith, Challinor; Lees, Caldwell and Taylor. The home team lost the toss and kicked off with the wind and sun against them. The visitors made a run down ,the field, and forced a corner, which was not improved upon. From the goal kick the ball was taken to the visitors' 'quarters, and some good defensive play was shown. The home forwards continued to press, Taylor and Siddall hitting the uprights, and no score resulting. A temporary invasion by the visitors saw Kite leave his goal and clear easily, and Lees, with a low 'shot, beat the visitors' cus- todian. From the centre kick even play fol- lowed in midfield, until the home half-backs set their forwards going, and Challinor was suc- cessful in scoring a second goal. The visitors paid another visit into the home half, only to be driven back by Robinson, and a strong attack was made on the Visitors' goal, which resulted in Lees ',coring a third goal': Althoigh the ball was kept in the Mobberley half, no more scor- ing took place, and at half-time the score was in favour of the home team by three goals to nil. _ _ _ ,

On resuming, the visitors played up very strongly, and came very near to scoring, but were eventually driven back by the home .de- fenders. At the other end Lees had hard lines, two shots just skimming the bar. Caldwell was more successful and scored through a crowd of players. The home team were now all Over their opponents, and Lees added a fifth goal, Up to the finish the play was in the visitors' half, and When the final whistle blew the home team had won easily by five goals to nil.

At a special meeting of the Finance Com- mittee of the Liberal AssoCiation, held last night, Councillor Peacock, in view of his ap- proaching election as Mayor, resigned his posi- tion as chairman a the party. He was heartily
To be Let.
thanked for his services, and great regret was expressed at the loss his retirement will be to
the party. Councillor Wilkinson was elected acting. chairman during Councillor Peacock's Mayor. faty.
Miscellaneous.
Education.
A RECORD OF WHICH TO BF, PROUD.
Repeated by Request, with Corrected Details.
TEAM AND OFFICIALS.
Photograph by Burrell.

From left to right :—Back row: A. Norman (committee), J. Sheader (committee), J. Broadhurst, D. Slater, W. Burgess (secretary), J. Whittaker, H. Morris, G. Warren, E. Saunders (committee), and C. Harding (trainer). Middle row: T. Scarisbrick, P. Morris, A. Stretford (captain), S. Carter, G. Floyd, and J. Brandwood. • Front row: A. Ilorrocks, J. Gallop and F. Horrocks.

During the four seasons that the Ryland& Northern Union Rugby Club has been in exist- ence it has been favoured with success. During the first two seasons they were affiliated to the St. Helens and District League, and at the first time of asking were successful in winning the cup by 8 points to 3, their opponents being Stockton Heath. In the second season they again reached the final, but were beaten at St. Helens by the White Rose to the extent of 8 points to 5. As the fortunes of the club were increasing, they embarked into the Second Divi- sion of the Manchester League in their third season, and distinguished themselVes by going through the competition with only one defeat. That year saw them run into the final for the Lancashire Junior Cup Competition, when they received their dismissal at the hands of the White Star, a Runcorn club, who only won after a hard struggle. The Manchester and District Shield and the Warrington Works Competition
also came into their hands that season, which was one to be proud of. MANCHESTER LEAGUE CHAMPIONS.

-- Last season, as champions of the Second Divi- sion of the Manchester League, they, passed into the First Division, and, after having had the Championship well in hand all along, they, in one season, passed from the Championship of the Second to the Championship of the First Division. They also won the Manchester and District Shield, running through the season with only two defeats.

The prospects for this season are as rosy as any of the others, when, so far, defeat has only once fell upon, them—and that in a friendly game. The success of the team is a credit to the town, and more especially to their works, where everyone of the players is employed. The play of several of the members has from time to time attracted the attention of prominent Northern Union Clubs, and Hennessey, Leah, and Bramhall have been, respectively, induced to throw in their lot with Salford, Swinton, and Warrington. Mr. Burgess is the best of secre- taries.

div.head: FRIENDLY SOCIETY SCHEME FOR THE
div.p: FRIENDLY SOCIETY SCHEME FOR THE

MAYOR'S SUNDAY. The Mayor-elect is to have a unique escort to-morrow week, when he attends the Parish Church on Mayor's Sunday. Councillor P. Pea- cock has been a prominent member of the Friendly Society movement for many years, and
is brethren in the different Orders fee7l that

his selection as Chief 'Magistrate shoulld be greeted by them as a tribute to the movement. All the Orders will be represented in the proces- sion, and at the church, and this will be the first occasion upon which members of the Friendly Societies in Warrington have officially participated in the function. At a conference held in the Town Hall on Thursday evening it was unanimously decided to take part in the procession. Bro. and Coun- cillor Peacock presided, and amongst those pre- sent were: Messrs. Clegg and Edgar, Shepherds; Thorniley and Chrimes, Foresters; W. Bibby and E. Allen, Druids; Fearnley, Rechabites; Walsh, Smalley and Sutton, Buffaloes; J. Ridge, Free Gardeners; F. Webster, Manchester ,TJAity of Oddfellows; and Mr. T. P. Bradshaw, who acted as secretary. Each society was asked to nominate, as early as possible, two marshals to act under Mr. T. P, Bradshaw, who was appointed Chief Marshal.

div.head: Order of the Procession.
div.p: Order of the Procession.

It was decided, as a compliment to ouncillor Peacock, that his society, the Foresters, should lead the Friendly Society part of the procession, followed by the Buffaloes, with their band. The remaining positions were balloted for, and the result was that the other Orders will follow in this order: National Independent Order of Odd- fellows, Free Gardeners, Druids, Shepherds, Grand United Order of Oddfellows, Rechabites, and the Manchester Unity of Oddfellows. The members meet at the Town Hall at 9.45 a.m., and it is hoped that at least 1,000 will _ _
attend. If more can come all the better, as the societies feel that the event should be made a red-letter day in their history.

div.head: SELECTION OF MAYOR AM) ALDERMEN.
div.p: SELECTION OF MAYOR AM) ALDERMEN.
Lively Scenes at Council Meeting.
A special meeting of the Council was held on Wednesday for the purpose of rehearsing the proceedings of the annual meeting to be held on Monday. The Mayor presided over a full attendance.

div.head: SELECTION OF MAYOR.
div.p: SELECTION OF MAYOR.

The name of Councillor Peter Pea.caock was agreed to unanimously, many members on both sides warmly supporting the nomination. Councillor PEAcocx thanked the members for their vote and expressed his appreciation of the honour conferred uP011,11411, and appealed for the co-operation and assistance of the members in the discharge of his duties. The Mayor-elect intimated that the Mayor had consented to act as Deputy-Mayor, and that the Rector had expressed his willingness to act as his Chaplain.

div.head: SELECTION OF ALDERMEN,
div.p: SELECTION OF ALDERMEN,

On the names of the five retiring Aldermen being submitted for re-election, a lively debate arose, not so much with regard to the indivi- duals concerned, but upon the wide question as to the manner of the election of Aldermen.

Several Aldermen protested against "person- ally insulting references," and claimed the re- spect which age and long service entitled some of them to receive. In the face of the stubbornness of some of the members, who were invited, but declined' to name the members to -whom they objected or to submit additional names, the names of the five retiring and selected Aldermen were not put to the vote.

div.head: HARDY ANNUAL.
div.p: A HARDY ANNUAL.
The hardy annual of Standing Orders was again the subject of much criticism, the object Of two of the . members being to enlarge the scope of debate.

div.head: COMMITTEES.
div.p: THE COMMITTEES.
The Standing Orders were then agreed to, and the committees appointed, the only alterations being as follows:

Co-un-c-illo-ainClley was placed.on the Finance and Estate Committee in the place. of Council- lor Osborne, who retired. Councillor Lindley was also added to the Museum Committee. ouncillors Gough and Henshall were placed on the Cemetery Committee in the places of, Councillors Locker and Shaw.

div.head: Railway Official Honoured.
div.p: Railway Official Honoured.

The celebration of an interesting event in local railway circles was held at the Royal Oak Hotel, Bridge-street, on Saturday evening. Mr. A. E. Cresswell, late foreman at the Locomotive Sheds, Dallam, was presented with a case of cutlery, suitably inscribed, and a knife cleaner, and also a gold bangle for Mrs. Cresswell, on ,the occasion of his promotion to the locomotive sheds at Patricroft. There was a large gather- ing, including several local officials of the L. and N.-W. Railway, amongst whom were Mr. Thomasson successor to Mr. Cresswell, Mr. Gordon, stltionmaster, and Mr. Singleton, of .the Traffic Department. Mr. John Brandwood proved a very capable chairman.i The Presen- tation was made by Mr. John Richardson, the oldest driver at the sheds, and he voiced - the feelings, of local railwaymen when he spoke of the great esteem and respect in which Mr. Cresswell was held. He was cordially supported by Messrs. W. Taylor and J. R. Palmer, the for- mer of whom made a very spirited speech. Mr. Cresswell, in responding, stated that it had been his sole desire to deal with the men in a fair and equitable way during the time he had been with them. The musical part of the pro- gramme was thoroughly enjoyed, the songs by Messrs. H. Bennett, W. Rigby, H. Harrison and Leigh being all well rendered and greatly, appre- ciated. Mr. E. Hassall gave a clarinet solo, and Mr.. Gilbert RoUghley two humorous songs, his singing of "Wee Deoch and Doris" bring- ing him an encore. Two choruses by the L. and N.-W. Glee Party were greatly enjoyed.
THE HANDBALL LEAGUE.
Warrington Gymnasium V. Royal Liver.

_ This League match was played at Liverpool on Thursday. The game opened at a brisk pace and it was not long before the Warrington team Opened the scoring, a good pass from Bibby enabling Jolley to !core for the champions with a fine shot. Sanders soon afterwards added a second goal., The Warrington team were having all the play and further goals were scored by Jolly and Sanders. Half-time arrived with the score four goals to nil in Warrington's favour. The Liverpool team showed some improvement in the second half, but were no match for the visitors, who added six more goals to their score, Bibby (1) and Sanders (5) being the scorers. Sanders, the Warrington centre-for- ward, played a fine game and bagged seven goals.

div.head: PUBLIC AMUSEMENTS.
div.p: PUBLIC AMUSEMENTS.
"THE PRIDE OF BYZANTIA "AT THE ROYAL COURT.

It is not often that so much laughter is crowded into two hours as the "Pride of Byzantia " has been causing twice nightly at the Boyal Cotirt Theatre this week. It is not the first time the " comedy revue" has visited Warrington, and ita reputation was sufficient to fill the house from the first night onward. Sammy Blenkinsop Ira Yorkshire, in the person of Mr. Will Lindsay, although he is sometimes on the extravagant side in playing the fool, is extremely funny and keeps the house in one continuous .roar of laughter. His mother (Miss Lucy Murray) and Sarah Ann, his mother's maid-of-all-work (Miss Madge Soutter), give him capable 'assistance, the three working 'together with admirable effect. Miss Mabel Medrow makes an ideal Princess and Sings her songs in clear and melodious' fashion. Little Mary O'Hara, a London waif, shows rare ability in one so young, both, in elocution and dancing; and the singing and dancing of six other little girls make quite a feature of the evening's entertainment. The other artistes all do well, while the scenery and stage effects more than justify the description of the play--." an autumn pantomime." There is sure to be a big house to-night. "ONLY A MILL GIRL" •
This popular drama will be presented twice nightly next week and should draw large houses. As the title suggests, it deals with life in a cotton .factory.

div.head: RAGTIME AT THE HIPPODROME.
div.p: RAGTIME AT THE HIPPODROME.

Mr. Herbert Landed: and Company have scored a success with the original playlet "The Son of a Jew" this week. Mr. Landeck plays the part of Nathan .Cohen, the money lender, who saves his son from marrying an adven- turess, in a capital manner, whilst Mr. Howard Brenan is well placed U.S Charles Cowan, the irresponsible Oxford student, who is infatuated by Mrs. Sinclair, a character which is under- taken by Miss Gwynne Warren with distinct *success._ The other members of the' company also play their parts well. Gordon and Elgin give an excellent exhibition of ragtime dancing, which is very popular. Frank Powell is a char- acter patter comedian with a host of new gags and side-splitting stories, who is equally funny as "The' Porter" and the "confidential' post- man." Leigh Bros., are smart entertainers, who introduce gymnastics and comedy in the bil- liard saloon. Constance' Mori is a charming dancer, and her Chinese dancing, as well as her vocal items, are most effective. Bert Castle is as popular as ever with his catchy songs and scores with his "steamer" \number. Lilian Farrar appears in a charming song scena, "Bubbles," and is loudly applauded. Thorn- bury is a clever lightning painter and intro- duces ventriloquism in a capital entertainment.

div.head: RAGTIME COMPETITION:
div.p: RAGTIME COMPETITION:

The ragtime dancing competition promoted by Gordon and Elgin has been a success and there have been many competitors for the prizes, amounting to £15.. The displays given by the " locals " have been very •creditable. The promoters have given instructions to com- petitors throughout the week.

div.head: NEXT WEEK'S ATTRACTIONS.
div.p: NEXT WEEK'S ATTRACTIONS.

A great Asiatic novelty, "` The slave Dealers," will be presented next week by Master Mirza Colem and • performers. The turn will be a spectacular one,and various gymnastic feats will be introduced. Other turns will be Harry Nelson, comedian; Renaud Lockwood and Co:, in "Backing the Gee-gees " ; Richard Finberg, the popular actor; Kisbey, the call-boy; Lily Hill, the Lancashire nightingale; and Dorma Ntorgan, comedienne.

div.head: BAND OF HOPE UNION. Annual Meeting of the Warrington
div.p: BAND OF HOPE UNION. Annual Meeting of the Warrington
Council.

The annual meeting of the Council of the above Union was held in Cairo-street School- room on Thursday. Mrs. James Dodds pre- sided over a good attendance of representatives from the various societies affiliated with the Union.

Mr. F. Gandy, hon. sec., submitted the report of the Executive Committee, which showed that a large amount of useful work had been done amongst the children during the past year. Mr. R. Pierce Williams presented the treas- urer's report, proving that the funds of the Union were in a very satisfactory condition. Mrs. James Dodds was unanimously re-elected president of the Union. In accepting the posi- tion for another year, Mrs. Dodds expressed her pleasure in working for the temperance cause, and said she was proud to be identified with the groat army of Band of Hope workers. Vice-presidents were chosen as under :—Revs. J. Yonge, J. S. Chedburn, E. Morgan, W. A. Beckett, H. Middlewood, H. Ogden, H. Wil- liamson, W. T. Jaye, Parry Jones, T. T. James, A. J. Chessum, Mrs. Simpson, Miss B. Dutton, Mrs. E. V. Walker, Mrs. W. J. Walker, Mrs. Thos. Owen, Mr. A. Ifounfield, Mr. W. Clat- worthy, Mr. Ben Few, Mr. Henry Thornton and Mr. Lawes (Police Court Missionary). Mr. R. Pierce Williams was re-elected hon. treasurer, and Mr. F. Gandy hon. secretary, for the 12th year. Several members spoke of Mr. Gandy's invaluable work to the union. Other appointments were: Hon. assistant sec- retary, Mr. J. E. Pardoe; Press secretary, Mr. G. Whitfield; auditors, Messrs. J. Whitmore and J. Hamblett; stock-takers, Mrs. Whitmore, Messrs. J. Hamblett and J. Whitmore; stock- keepers, Mrs. G. Shaw and Mrs. Nurse, regis- trar, Mr. W. Watkins; ordanrst and accom- panist, Mr. T. Tanner; musical conductor, Mr. A. Spruce; Apresentatives to Lancashire and Cheshire Band of Hope Union, Messrs. W. Wat- kins, E. Andrews and T. Dunabin.

Arrangements have been made for special ser- vices in all Sunday Schools on Temperance Sunday to-morrow, and after a service a meeting to be held in the Co-operative Hall at 8 p.m. The meetings of the Temperance Guild for Senior Members are to be held periodically dur- ing the winter months. _ _
A resolution of sympathy with Miss Maud Kirkland, Temperance "queen," in her illness, and praying for her speedy recovery, was passed during the evening.
The- meeting was full of vigour and speaks well for the success of the coming winter's work.

div.head: ARTS AND CRAFTS.
div.p: ARTS AND CRAFTS.
Fine Pictures Shown; but Poor Display
in Graftworke

The Old Academy was converted into a mini- ature art gallery during the week. The Arts and Crafts Exhibition was held there on Wed- nesday and Thursday, and the exhibits were of particular interest to Warringtonians. While the display as neat .and compact, and con- tained many interesting features, it was to be regretted that the crafts section was so indiffer- ent, and the question became: Could not this be omitted in the future? Pictures were the strong feature, yet the ex- hibits were•not so numerous as could have been desired. Included in the pictures hung on be- half of our local artists was a 'beautiful animal study by Mr. Lewis, who excels in this class of work. Portraiture was the feature of Miss Ridgway's work, and she presented several charming specimens of her art. Particularly good was the portrait of her mother, and skie seemed to reach the climax in her ,art with "Peggy," a charming tinted pencil drawing. Mr. C. Mawson had an interesting collection of sketches and oils. " The Derelict" was an admirable piece of pencil work. The cloud effects were particularly striking. Miss Broad- bent's water-colours were real works of art. Studies of Grappenhali were very fine, and she seemed to have discovered and reproduced re- markably picturesque features in the picture labelled Crosfield's Works." Mr. Archer hay. ward's style attracted attention, and he pre- sented rural scenes with remarkable colour effects. Successful pictures were also forwarded by Mr. Oswald Garside, Miss Margaret Davies and Mr. W. N. Hutchings. Lace, &c., was a particularly fine exhibition, and amongst the exhibitors were, Mrs. C. E. Parker, Miss Fairclough, and Miss Harvey. Other features proved attractive.
The exhibition was openedon Wednesday by Alderman Bennett, in the. absence, tirrough illness, of Mrs. Rylands. Miss Broadbent pre- sided.

div.head: SEVENPENCE FOR 311,
div.p: SEVENPENCE FOR 311,
Policeman's Luck _with an Alleged
Gambling Machine.
MACHINES TO BE REMOVED.

Plunging with thr€73pence in testing an alleged gambling machine in a Warrington shop a policeman found that he had gained seven- pence. Others of his brothers in blue, were, however, not so fortunate, and they found themselves losers. These facts came to light during the hearing of an interesting case at the Warrington Borough Police Court on Tuesday, before Coun- cillor 11. Roberts (in the chair), Colonel Edel- sten and Mr. C. Jackson Holmes, when charges of keeping houses for the purposes of gaming were brought in against Hey Gr,een, Knutsford road;Cooper, Mersey-street; John . jui w Stockton, Mersey-street; Thomas Burke, Napier-street; Esther Annie, Buckley, Church- street; Jane West, Buttermarket-street; Louis Manfredi, Sankey-street; John Hughes, Bew- sey-street ; Edward Horrocks, Winwick-road ; Stephen Raffo, Pinner's-brow; William Critch- ley, Lythgoes-lane; and Elizabeth Mitchell, Winwick-street. The Chief Constable stated that the sum- monses were issued under Section 4 of the Gain- ing House Act of 1854. The proceedings were taken in connection with an instrument which the police alleged to be a gaming instrument.
To Play the Game.

_ There were twelve boles in the machine, and to manipulate it a penny had to be placed in the slot, which released a small ball at the, bottom. By a hammer arrangement the opera- tor propelled the ball round the disc and it depended upon which hole the ball went into whether the operator received anything or not. The returns from the machine were in the form of cheques, which the successful operator ex- changed for articles in the shop to the value of 2d. or 3d. The Chief Constable' said that the Bench would be perfectly satisfied that it was a gaming machine. In the case of Mrs. Green, who kept a greengrocer's shop in Snutsford-road, a police officer visited the shop on October 18th and witnessed two boys try their luck, but both lost their pennies. The officer then told the defendant that, in his opinion, it was a gaming instrument, and in trying his luck the officer got a return of 2d. for his 6d. He then told Mrs. Green that he would have to report it, whereupon the defendant said: I have no desire to have them in my shop if it is im- proper." She further asked the policeman to remove it. The police tested the machine several times, and, as a matter of fact, one constable got' 7d. in return for 3d.
"These Ingenious. Machines."

Mr. Arthur Browne, solicitor, who appeared for the twelve defendants and the firm to whom the machines belonged, said that under the Act of Parliament they had the right to go to the Quarter Sessions, which would Cost the town a considerable amount. It was a very important matter to the owners of these ingenious mach- ines. , Some months ago there was a case tried at -Cardiff, when the Recorder, in spite of cer- tain decisions of which they were aware, found that the machines did not come under this Act of Parliament, and as a result the machines were introduced into 20 various towns, and this was the first place where there had been an objection to -them. The machines were .not the property of the persons summoned, but were the property of a firm who had these machines in all sorts. and kinds of shops. They , were first introduced into the public- houses, but, in consequence of certain reports, the Chief Constable intervened and they were put into the shops.

Eighty in Warrington. He ventured to submit that those cases would be met if the firm undertook to take all the machines out of the town within seven days. Those proceeded against were not the only people who had the machines on the premises. The Chief Constable: There are 80 in the town. Mr. Browne, continuing, said his clients would pay the costs of the summonses. He submitted that the defendants did not know that the machines were illegal. ' Ultimately the Bench agreed to the course proposed by Mr. Browne, Councillor Roberts. the chairman, remarking that the owners of the machines knew perfectly well they were illegdl, and the Bench thought the defendants had been misled. They were sorry the owners were not in Court. The defendants would have to pay Bs. 6d. costs in each case. They were bound to express the opinion that the 'game was a game' of chance. The Bench did not want it to be thought they had upheld What was really against the law.

div.p: BILLIARDS.
SENIOR CONSERVATIVE CLUB TEAM COMPETITION.

Judging from the splendid attendances that witnessed the opening matches in the above competition at the Sankey-street club, it is quite evident the members are taking excep- tional interest in this new venture, and really the two games already played have been well worth watching, and created plenty of excite- ment, which speaks well for the handicapping- The committee are supplying rolled geld 'watches to the ultimate winning team, so that the winners will be well repaid for theit efforts- It was rather unfortunate that Fairfield NO. should be without their popular captain, P• Cooper (he being indisposed), but they put up a good fight against the St. Austin's No. 3 team, as the result rested on the last game, in which A. Bailie f theaiolie m favouritea.deagre teams,ateffortLatchford Ltaotewionr,d so but. Atli; Kenworthy compiled a couple of good brealzP late on in the game, and this put paid to the Fairfield iteA. fell at the first hurdle against a team main.,7 composed of what. one would describe as -"e7.- ing platers." However, great credit is due J. E. Harrison's men on their victory over team, which which included a couple of the Seniors' first team. Corradine fairly surprised the critics by his good play against Bert Simpson, and con- sidering the .big handicap, H. Parkes and G. Marshall did very well to win their games. Re- sults :—St. Austin's No. 3, 487; Fairfield No. 1, 429. Latchford No. 2, 483; Latchford No. 1, 433.

TRIBUTE TO THE LATE JOSEPH ARMITAGE. Joseph Armitage; Gorsey-lane, who died last week at the age of 32, leaving a widow and four young children, after having suffered from typhoid fever for a fortnight, was buried in Sunday. He was a noted Warrington League billiard player, and played for Rylands' Recrea- tion team, which went through last season los- ing only one match. Ry-lands' Club were repre- sented at the funeral by Messrs. J. Jeffrey (car tam). W. IL Phillips (secretary), A. Kenyon and E. P. Saunders. ,Mr. J. Craik, hon. sec. of the League, also attended.

Any Insured person who desires to be attended after the 11th January, 1914, by a Practitioner OTHER than the Practitioner who is attending him in the current year, or to obtain treatment by any of the methods referred to in the said Regulations OTHER than that which be adopted for the current year, shall make application to the Committee not later than the 11th day of DECEMBER, 1913.
